statements.t: (NYSE: CHD) today announced that the Company exceeded its third quarter outlook with stronger than forecasted sales and earnings growth.
Net sales increased 1.0% to $1,602 million in the third quarter, exceeding the Company’s outlook of a 1% decline and reflecting the benefits of the 2025 strategic portfolio actions.
Organic sales grew 5.1%, well above the Company’s 3% outlook, with growth across all three divisions, driven primarily by volume growth of 4.6%, as well as positive price and mix of 0.5%.
In the third quarter, our leading brands once again increased share driven by innovation, distribution wins, and our targeted marketing investments.

The strength of our brand portfolio, combined with our targeted 2025 strategic portfolio actions, has enhanced the focus on our growth initiatives and reinforces our confidence as we enter the fourth quarter of 2026 and into 2027.
We are raising our 2026 outlook for sales and tightening our outlook for earnings per share.
Third quarter Adjusted EPS of $0.92 increased 13.6% versus last year and exceeded the Company’s outlook of $0.89.
Stronger-than-expected sales drove earnings growth versus our outlook and supported incremental SG&A investments and incentive compensation.
The Company continues to expect approximately $1.175 billion of cash from operations for full-year 2026.”
The Company expects full-year capital expenditures to be approximately $125 million or 2% of sales.
“We are confident that our relentless focus on innovation will continue to drive industry-leading growth, distribution gains at shelf, and market share expansion.
Our improved sales outlook reflects the strength of our operating fundamentals, which underpin our volume growth, market share gains and gross margin expansion.
Volume growth, productivity, tariff refunds and favorable mix from our acquisitions and portfolio actions are expected to more than offset higher inflation, transportation and tariff-related costs.
“Marketing as a percentage of sales is expected to be approximately 11% of sales reflecting the Company’s continued commitment to brand investment.

“We continue to expect SG&A as a percentage of sales to remain above 2025 levels, reflecting the impact of the TOUCHLAND and MISS MOUTH’S acquisitions and our targeted investments in growth initiatives, AI, ecommerce and our international business.
“Our adjusted tax rate is expected to be approximately 21%.
“We now expect full-year reported EPS to increase approximately 20%.
We also expect Adjusted EPS growth for 2026 of 7%, tightening the range from our prior expectation of 6% to 8%.
“Our Cash flow from operations outlook remains approximately at $1.175 billion.

We will continue to pursue acquisitions that meet our strict criteria, with an emphasis on fast-moving consumable products, similar to the successful THERABREATH, HERO, TOUCHLAND and MISS MOUTH’S acquisitions.
“For the fourth quarter, we expect reported sales decline of approximately 0.5%, driven entirely by the strategic portfolio actions taken in 2025.
We expect organic sales growth of approximately 4.0%¹ and continued gross margin expansion.
Overall adjusted EPS is expected to increase 17% to 19% versus last year. ¹ Similar to past years, when we have strong business performance, we prioritize investing for the future.
Our fourth quarter investments will focus on driving future growth and targeted AI capabilities.
We look forward to sharing our first formal update on these initiatives at our January investor meeting.”
We believe our existing tariff cost exposure will be mitigated through the above-mentioned actions, future additional supply chain efforts and surgical pricing .
The Company intends to invest refund proceeds in consumer-facing activities and to offset inflationary pressures.

We paid $300.0 cash at closing and deferred payment of $25.0 of the purchase price with $10.0 paid in the third quarter of 2026, and an additional $5.0 expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026 related to required post-closing activities of the seller.

We do not anticipate that current economic conditions will adversely affect our ability to comply with the financial covenant in the Credit Agreement because we currently are, and anticipate that we will continue to be, in compliance with the maximum leverage ratio requirement under the Credit Agreement.
